question.problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given below.

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=2$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.1$ | $0.4$ |

Given that $\textrm{E}[X] = 3$ and $\textrm{E}[Y] = 2.2,$ find the covariance matrix for $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
For two random variables $X$ and $Y,$ the covariance matrix $\Sigma$ is given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14274885/assets/c457df4f5450340a178e0f8c951ece5643acb78295bd98fe935d0a81933a3112.svg)

Recall that the variance of a random variable $X$ is determined by the formula

$$
\textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm{E}[X^2] - \textrm{E}[X]^2,
$$

and the covariance of two random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by the formula

$$
\textrm{Cov}[X,Y] = \textrm{E}[XY] - \textrm{E}[X] \cdot \textrm{E}[Y].
$$

First, let's find the marginal mass functions for $X$ and $Y.$ These are given by the row and column totals, respectively.

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=3$ | $f_X$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=2$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ | $0.5$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.1$ | $0.4$ | $0.5$ |
| $f_Y$ | $0.4$ | $0.6$ | $1$ |

Now, we can find $\textrm{Var}[X].$ If $X$ is defined on a support $S_X,$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}{x}^{2}\cdot {f}_{X}(x) \\  & ={2}^{2}\cdot 0.5+{4}^{2}\cdot 0.5 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =10-{3}^{2} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, if $Y$ is defined on a support $S_Y,$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{Y}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{y}}{y}^{2}\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & ={1}^{2}\cdot 0.4+{3}^{2}\cdot 0.6 \\  & =5.8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]-\text{E}[Y]^{2} \\  & =5.8-{2.2}^{2} \\  & =0.96.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, let's find $\textrm{Cov}[X,Y].$ By the rule of the lazy statistician, we find $\textrm{E}[XY]{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}xy\cdot f(x,y) \\  & =(2)(1)f(2,1)+(4)(1)f(4,1)+(2)(3)f(2,3)+(4)(3)f(4,3) \\  & =2\cdot 0.3+4\cdot 0.1+6\cdot 0.2+12\cdot 0.4 \\  & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the covariance formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =7-3\cdot 2.2 \\  & =0.4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the covariance matrix is given by
